summary: test22 turns a 397-variable/171-equality model into 213 variables with 171 ranged rows by per-row pivot elimination, 13 fixed-zero removals and one equal-cost aggregation. The analysis established that whole map in 21 turns / 643 s, but the 199 KB, 4647-obligation certificate (0.124 s to prepare, 4.90 ms to verify) had to be reassembled from MPS text: no typed, range-aware readback exists in the bound toolchain, the analysis's lifts are prose (the aggregate lift is even nonlinear), and the claim is a 211-coordinate projection plus one affine observation that only the kernel's v5 affine_projection capability can carry.
claims: 4 projection claims = {forward,reverse} x {integer,LP}: source 397 vars/171 equalities -> target 213 vars/171 ranged rows, objective Equal, inverse null. 4647 obligations (1139/1349/981/1178), 51683 work units, no branches.

211 coordinate projections (retained original names) + 1 affine observation: input x142+x145 = output agg107. No bijection is claimed because aggregation discards the split between two equal-cost columns (both [0,4], cost 1001).

Forward claims prove each target interval [b_r-U_r, b_r] from source equality r minus the pivot bound; reverse claims prove source pivot [0,U_r] from the target ranged-row endpoints (171 RowUpper + 171 RowLower).
Objective identity is absorbed by fixed column objconst=1 with cost -3397586999999310018947800000094739/1000000000000000000000000000 plus 171 RowEq terms scaled by the pivot cost.
All four deliberate mutations are rejected: wrong_offset, missing_pivot_bound, wrong_recovery, missing_sum_observation (exit 2, status INVALID).

Reverse block: map 397 entries (171 pivot expressions, 13 zeros, 2 split halves, retained identities); checks 1349 = 171 RowUpper + 171 RowLower + 422 var bounds + 422 Exact + 158 VarInt + 5 Local.

Kernel runs all exit 0: canonical source, canonical target, assemble, verify; every artifact hash-bound in preparation.json.
agent_manual_work: Parsed the MPS twice (token parser plus independent fixed-field transcription), then wrote a separate artifact decoder and a 7010-byte verify.py: 171 symbolic row identities, the objective identity, 200 lifted points, 34200 row-bound checks, 855 boundary probes.
Hand-wrote output/reformulated.mps (22938 bytes) with a decimal_exact formatter asserting every emitted rational has a terminating decimal expansion.
Enumerated 7 hypotheses: private-pivot elimination and equal-cost aggregation accepted; integer bound tightening, duplicate rows/columns, equality dependence, component decomposition rejected.
The report's reconstruction is nonlinear (x142=min(4,g), x145=g-x142); the certificate instead splits g/2,g/2 and leans on the [0,8] aggregate bound.
21 turns, 643 s wall, 0 failed calls; 17 eval cells, 44781 chars of eval code; kernel verification of the finished certificate is 4.90 ms.

friction: The bound binary (sha de58aded...) rejects rpx export-model with INVALID usage exit 2 even though docs/API.md:94-105 documents it, and inspect-model returns counts only, so typed model access was hand-written at least three times.

RowUpper for a ranged G row means upper = rhs+range (crates/core/src/verify.rs:180 uses row.upper) but prep-side row_fact builds it from rhs; the case had to override it, and an alternative premise fails only as a generic obligation.

Handoff cost: only 3 keys of the 142080-byte audit.json are read (tools/prepare_test22.py:43); row_edits[].lift is prose and the aggregate lift is the nonlinear min(4,g), so the analysis's own reconstruction could not be certified as written.
The audit already lists new_interval/new_range per row, yet the preparer recovers intervals from the target text, so 171 rows x 2 endpoints = 342 Lin steps re-derive rhs-U_r and b_r.

All four mutations yield only {status:INVALID, message:'...obligation 108'}; the claim index is absent across 4 claims of ~1000 obligations each, so attribution is unassertable (tools/prepare_test22.py:117 checks status only).
